en: The Vajraśekhara-sūtra: The Dharmakāya Mudrās and Mantras of One Hundred and Eight Honored Ones of Vairocana,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha and the Upādhyāya Wuxing.

VAJRA-NĪTI NITI HŪṂ SVĀHĀ. Vajramātā: “OṂ VAJRAHA HA HA HA HO HŪṂ HO HŪṂ SVĀHĀ. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraguhyaka:

Having spoken these seal-mudrās and mantra-syllables of the Vajra Honored One’s siddhi, one abides in great tranquility, detached from all mental activity. Within the circle of the ūrṇā-kośa of the Moon-Love Samādhi, one clearly contemplates them appearing in succession; the vajra-great-maṇi-wish-fulfilling jewels of all Tathāgatas are of a single dharma-nature, a single true dharma-realm, and a single flavor of suchness—neither coming nor going, signless and unconditioned—the pure dharma-body illuminating the ocean of perfect stillness.
Thus, these eight hundred adamantine phrases, originally arising from the single dharma of samādhi,
contemplate the gate of non-duality of true suchness, whereby one enters the ocean of the Tathāgata’s perfect quiescence.
Skillfully knowing the phrases of emergence and entry, and all the rituals for yogic siddhi;
practicing the myriad deeds of enlightenment in a single instant, one is forever freed from all beginningless delusions.
The eighty-four thousand sublime Dharma gates Enter through the single-syllable mantra and mudrā;
Their merits, as vast as the sands of the Ganges, are beyond calculation, Universally delivering sentient beings without limit or end.
The emptiness of persons, the emptiness of phenomena, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the one true dharma-realm is primordially empty.
All the Tathāgatas, the guides of the ten directions who have attained perfect enlightenment, rely entirely upon these adamantine verses.
Each phrase, each seal, and each mantra are first arrayed from the heart-cakra at the crown of the head;
they flow to the two shoulders, the left and right ears, and the tips of both nostrils; they are poured into the *ūrṇā-kośa*, the hairline, and the space between the eyebrows;
then to the neck, the two cheeks, the point between the brows, the lips, teeth, eyes, palate, and the center of the throat.
The two arms and ten fingers are the pāramitās; The chest, the back, and the two pairs of feet, The navel wheel, and the Vajra-palace above it, The Heart-King dwells within the Moon-Light Treasury.
Adorned everywhere with jeweled banners and precious parasols, It is signless, without coming, and without going.
Second is the Lotus-Vajra Lamp; at the site of the nose, the Joyful Play of Scented Unction, one sits upon the siddhi-vajra-maṇḍala.
With pure radiance like the full moon, one should thus sequentially visualize the hundred and eight [deities] of body and mind until they are clear and pure.
Sudden realization of the secret seal of bodhi, Wandering freely upon the path of nirvāṇa;
Having established the worldly *siddhis* to completion, One then relies on empowerment to perform recitation.
Truly a supreme son born of the Tathāgata, One fulfills the pure Dharma of the Single Vehicle.
When the hosts of the celestial Māra armies saw this person, they joined their palms and proclaimed him the Savior of the World.
They further spoke of the Unshakable Vajra Wisdom, the ultimate locus where the Buddha’s Dharma-body is realized.
As stated in the "Paramārtha" chapter of the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, they gazed upon him as if looking toward a Teacher of the World.
Transmitting the secret gate of the Bhagavān, the eight classes of beings, nāgas, and devas all look up with reverence.

When wishing to walk, sit, or recite mantras, whether exiting or entering [the state of purity], through the signs of speech, hold a golden *vajra* in the mouth; with the two eyes as *maṭha*, eliminate past obstacles.
Constantly contemplating sitting within the bright moon-mirror, Expansively pervading the dharma-realm with the measure of empty space;
The mind attains mastery, free from coming or going, As merit is constantly practiced and universally dedicated.
The Gate of Entering the Contemplation of the Dharmakāya:
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, The Vajra-Apex of all Tathāgatas.
Within the site of enlightenment of the Great Dharmadhātu, With single-minded contemplation, one clearly perceives.
The Wondrous High Mountain is extraordinary and most rare; By means of spiritual powers and holy strength, one ascends its peak.
Surveying the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, They are as if a mani-jewel held within the palm.
Awakening to this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, One dwells securely on the auspicious ground of the Tathāgata.
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, the Vajra King of all Tathāgatas,
the sovereign radiance of the ocean of quiescence, the supreme one praised by the awakened ones of the ten directions,
whose merit as vast as the sands of the Ganges is fully perfected, who is signless, pure, and equal to true emptiness.
Awakening to this samādhi and the seal of bodhi, One dwells securely in the auspicious ground of the Tathāgata.
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, The vajra-peak of all Tathāgatas;
His crown-mark is boundless and invisible, Transcending the ocean of worlds in the ten directions.
The mani-jewels of a thousand crags and myriad valleys Reflect within vessels of lapis lazuli and crystal;
Awakening to these treasures of the ten-thousandfold images through this samādhi, One dwells securely upon the auspicious ground of the Tathāgata.
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, the adamantine life-force of all Tathāgatas, whose lifespan is infinite and incalculable.
Upon the land of Sukhāvatī, where water-birds and forest trees abound, beings are born with a sudden rustle within the flowers; from within the pearls, the birds sing the melodies of the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva bathes in the waters of golden sand; in a single thought, they receive their prediction throughout the ten directions.
Realizing this swift and non-retrogressive contemplation, they dwell securely in the auspicious ground of the Tathāgata.
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, the vajra-throne of all Tathāgatas, the ocean-seal treasure of siddhis as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Upon it ascend the boundless Sugatas;
their radiant halos pervade the dharma-realm without obstruction, like the moon reflected in water or an image in a mirror.
A lion atop the head, filling all of space, with canopies of seven-jeweled golden lotuses and pearls;
by awakening to this samādhi-siddhi seal, one dwells securely in the auspicious ground of the Tathāgata.
I prostrate to Vairocana Buddha, The vajra-body of all Tathāgatas,
Pervading the entire dharma-realm without limit, Manifesting in response throughout the ten directions to fill all space.
He can manifest many bodies from a single body, And again manifest the form of a single body from many bodies.
Having a body and having marks is a provisional manifestation; Neither body nor mark is the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*).
Awakening to this samādhi is the palace of nirvāṇa; One thereby enters the auspicious ground of the Tathāgata.
